parity:secret-screenshot-send.evidence: Send mechanism EXISTS in TDLib: viewMessages takes source:MessageSource (td_api.tl:13230) and messageSourceScreenshot exists (td_api.tl:3234) — TGX uses this path. But Linux has no OS screenshot-detection API to trigger it: X11 exposes no screenshot-taken event; Wayland has no standard screenshot-detection protocol; no D-Bus signal from screenshot tools. Independently corroborated by lucid-softworks/react-native-linux Linux screen-capture doc (no portable detection signal; honest no-op). TDLib is UI-agnostic and cannot detect OS screenshots itself. Polling screenshot dirs is flaky (clipboard-only captures, custom paths) — rejected.

parity:secret-screenshot-block.evidence: No FLAG_SECURE equivalent on Linux: X11 any client can XGetImage the root window with no per-window opt-out (protocol fact); Wayland has no standard secure-surface protocol — wp-security-context-v1 is compositor-specific (GNOME mutter partial, sway/others no) and does not reliably block PipeWire/screen-cast capture. td_api.tl grep for secure/prevent/screenshot shows no window-security API (only story protect_content, server-side). TDLib does not do window management. Independently corroborated by the same Linux screen-capture doc (no portable secure-window hint; capture tools succeed regardless).

parity:secret-session-terminate.evidence: td_api.tl 1.8.67: secretChat (line 2816) = id, user_id, state, is_outbound, key_hash, layer — NO session id, NO auth-key linkage. session (line 9144) = capability flags only (can_accept_secret_chats), NO secret-chat linkage. Zero 'auth_key' fields anywhere in td_api.tl. Which auth-key a secret chat is bound to is server-side/internal state not exposed to clients; per-device E2E state means other sessions' secret chats are unknowable client-side anyway. No client-side join key exists, so the count cannot be computed. TGX shows no such count on session termination (its ClosingXSecretChats string is for bulk chat deletion).
